---
title: "Example 02 - BMI and smoking status (NHANES 2017-2018)"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
params:
  calculate_ss: false
---

This example reproduces the BMI analysis from the paper using R only. We compare
three smoking groups: never smokers (N), former smokers (F) and current smokers (C).

By default, we use the original non-rejection counts saved from our R analysis.
This avoids repeating 54,000 subsampling tests. Set `calculate_ss: true` to
run any comparisons that have not yet been saved as RDS files.

# 1. Libraries and data

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)
```

```{r data}
library(similaritystructure)
library(haven)
library(ggplot2)

# Download the original NHANES 2017-2018 files only once.
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)

files <- c("DEMO_J", "SMQ_J", "BMX_J")
url <- "https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/"

for (f in files) {
  path <- file.path("data", paste0(f, ".XPT"))
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    download.file(paste0(url, f, ".XPT"), path, mode = "wb")
  }
}

demo <- haven::read_xpt("data/DEMO_J.XPT")
smq  <- haven::read_xpt("data/SMQ_J.XPT")
bmx  <- haven::read_xpt("data/BMX_J.XPT")

demo <- as.data.frame(demo[, c("SEQN", "RIDAGEYR")])
smq  <- as.data.frame(smq[, c("SEQN", "SMQ020", "SMQ040")])
bmx  <- as.data.frame(bmx[, c("SEQN", "BMXBMI")])

# The paper includes adults aged 20 years or older.
dat <- merge(demo, smq, by = "SEQN")
dat <- dat[!is.na(dat$RIDAGEYR) & dat$RIDAGEYR >= 20, ]

# SMQ020: at least 100 cigarettes in life.
# SMQ040: current smoking frequency among those who answered yes.
dat$smoking <- NA_character_
dat$smoking[which(dat$SMQ020 == 2)] <- "Never"
dat$smoking[which(dat$SMQ020 == 1 & dat$SMQ040 == 3)] <- "Former"
dat$smoking[which(dat$SMQ020 == 1 & dat$SMQ040 %in% c(1, 2))] <- "Current"

dat <- dat[!is.na(dat$smoking), ]
dat$smoking <- factor(dat$smoking, levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current"))

# Keep missing BMI values at this stage to check the original group sizes.
dat <- merge(dat, bmx, by = "SEQN", all.x = TRUE)
classified <- table(dat$smoking)
available <- table(dat$smoking[is.finite(dat$BMXBMI)])

data.frame(Group = names(classified),
           Classified = as.integer(classified),
           Available_BMI = as.integer(available),
           Missing_BMI = as.integer(classified - available))

# The paper reports 5,569 classified participants (before excluding missing BMI).
expected <- c(Never = 3234L, Former = 1329L, Current = 1006L)
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(classified), as.integer(expected)))

# Only the 5,175 participants with a BMI value enter the analysis.
dat <- dat[is.finite(dat$BMXBMI), ]
groups <- split(dat$BMXBMI, dat$smoking)

summary_bmi <- data.frame(
  Group = names(groups),
  N = lengths(groups),
  Mean = sapply(groups, mean),
  SD = sapply(groups, sd)
)
print(summary_bmi, row.names = FALSE)

# Check that the means match those reported in the paper.
stopifnot(all(round(summary_bmi$Mean, 2) ==
              c(Never = 29.69, Former = 30.83, Current = 29.08)))
```

# 2. Welch tests and Cohen's d

We first reproduce the ordinary, unweighted comparisons between smoking groups.
These are descriptive analyses of the NHANES sample, not population estimates
using NHANES survey weights.

```{r tests}
pairs <- list("N-C" = c("Never", "Current"),
              "F-N" = c("Former", "Never"),
              "F-C" = c("Former", "Current"))

tests <- data.frame()

for (name in names(pairs)) {
  A <- groups[[pairs[[name]][1]]]
  B <- groups[[pairs[[name]][2]]]

  pooled_sd <- sqrt(((length(A) - 1)*var(A) +
                     (length(B) - 1)*var(B))/(length(A) + length(B) - 2))

  tests <- rbind(tests, data.frame(
    Comparison = name,
    Difference = mean(A) - mean(B),
    Cohen_d = (mean(A) - mean(B))/pooled_sd,
    p = t.test(A, B)$p.value
  ))
}

tests$p_Holm <- p.adjust(tests$p, method = "holm")
print(tests, row.names = FALSE, digits = 5)
```

# 3. Similarity structures

We keep the original analysis settings: 60 subsample sizes, 300 repetitions,
Welch's t-test, alpha = 0.05 and seed = 12345.

Importantly, subsampling is **with replacement**. Therefore, the evaluated
subsample size can exceed the number of observed participants. Resampling does
not, however, create new independent participants.

If calculate_ss is FALSE, the original empirical counts are loaded from
bmi_counts.csv and fitted again with the current package. This is fast and
uses the new binomial GAM. If calculate_ss is TRUE, any missing RDS results
are calculated and saved. Delete a saved RDS file to repeat that comparison.

```{r similarity-structures}
N_fin <- c("N-C" = 4500L, "F-N" = 1500L, "F-C" = 800L)
N_init <- 2L
num_N <- 60L
num_repet <- 300L
alpha <- 0.05
seed <- 12345L

# The CSV contains only the 180 original non-rejection counts.
count_file <- system.file("extdata", "bmi_counts.csv",
                          package = "similaritystructure")
if (!nzchar(count_file)) count_file <- "inst/extdata/bmi_counts.csv"
counts <- read.csv(count_file)

ss <- list()

for (name in names(pairs)) {
  file <- file.path("results", paste0("ss_bmi_", name, ".rds"))

  if (file.exists(file)) {
    # Use previously calculated results, when available.
    ss[[name]] <- readRDS(file)

  } else if (isTRUE(params$calculate_ss)) {
    # Full calculation: this takes time, so save each comparison separately.
    A <- groups[[pairs[[name]][1]]]
    B <- groups[[pairs[[name]][2]]]

    ss[[name]] <- similarity_structure(
      n1 = A, n2 = B,
      N_init = N_init, N_fin = N_fin[[name]],
      num_N = num_N, num_repet = num_repet,
      replace = TRUE, test = "t-test",
      alpha = alpha, seed = seed, plotting = FALSE
    )
    saveRDS(ss[[name]], file)

  } else {
    # Refit the cached counts without repeating the subsampling tests.
    empirical <- counts[counts$comparison == name, c("N", "num_nosig")]
    empirical$scaled <- empirical$num_nosig/empirical$num_nosig[1]
    attr(empirical, "num_repet") <- num_repet

    # This package helper is used only for refitting cached results.
    fitted <- similaritystructure:::smooth_fitting_Ns(
      N_init, N_fin[[name]], empirical,
      plotting = FALSE, num_repet = num_repet
    )
    ss[[name]] <- list(scaled_bn = empirical, simil_struct_Ns = fitted)
  }
}
```

# 4. Similarity sizes and similar effect probabilities

We calculate the similarity size from both the parametric fit and the
binomial GAM. For pS, the parametric fit is the primary result, as in the
original figure. The smoothing calculation is also shown for comparison.

```{r results}
order <- names(pairs)
ns <- data.frame(Comparison = order, Ns_fitting = NA_real_,
                 Ns_smoothing = NA_real_)

for (i in seq_along(order)) {
  fit <- ss[[i]]$simil_struct_Ns$fitting
  smooth <- ss[[i]]$simil_struct_Ns$smooth
  if (is.null(fit)) stop("Parametric fitting failed for ", order[i])
  ns$Ns_fitting[i] <- fit$Ns_fitting
  ns$Ns_smoothing[i] <- smooth$Ns_smooth
}

# Historical values, for comparison with the original MATLAB figures.
ns$Ns_original <- c(1258.2067, 352.9959, 160.7894)
print(ns, row.names = FALSE, digits = 6)

ps_fit <- ps_smooth <- matrix(NA_real_, 3, 3,
                              dimnames = list(order, order))

for (i in 1:3) {
  for (j in 1:3) {
    A <- ss[[i]]$simil_struct_Ns
    B <- ss[[j]]$simil_struct_Ns

    ps_fit[i, j] <- prob_effect(fitting_A = A$fitting,
                               fitting_B = B$fitting)
    ps_smooth[i, j] <- prob_effect(smooth_A = A$smooth,
                                 smooth_B = B$smooth)
  }
}

cat("pS - parametric fitting:\n")
print(ps_fit, digits = 5)
cat("pS - binomial smoothing:\n")
print(ps_smooth, digits = 5)
```

The smoothed SS is normalized over the evaluated finite range, whereas the
parametric SS has an infinite tail. For this reason, a smoothed pS may be
exactly zero when the other similarity size exceeds the finite range.
Such a zero must not be interpreted as a true zero probability.

# 5. Figures

## Similarity structures

```{r figure-ss}
curves <- data.frame()

for (name in order) {
  fit <- ss[[name]]$simil_struct_Ns$fitting
  curves <- rbind(curves, data.frame(
    Comparison = name, n = fit$vect_N_fit, Sn = fit$Sn
  ))
}

colors <- c("N-C" = "#2C5FDB", "F-N" = "#87B943", "F-C" = "#D74A46")

ggplot(curves, aes(x = n, y = Sn, color = Comparison)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(100, 1000, 10000)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  labs(x = "Subsample size (n)", y = "S(n)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Similarity sizes

```{r figure-ns}
ggplot(ns, aes(x = Comparison, y = Ns_fitting, fill = Comparison)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Ns_fitting, 1)), vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Similarity size (nS)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## pS matrix

Values below 0.05 are displayed as <0.05 in the figure; the numerical
matrix above keeps their full precision. pS is a descriptive comparison
probability, not a hypothesis-test p-value.

```{r figure-ps, fig.width=6.5}
ps_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(ps_fit))
names(ps_df) <- c("Comparison_A", "Comparison_B", "pS")
ps_df$Comparison_A <- factor(ps_df$Comparison_A, levels = order)
ps_df$Comparison_B <- factor(ps_df$Comparison_B, levels = rev(order))
ps_df$label <- ifelse(ps_df$pS < 0.05, "<0.05",
                      sprintf("%.3f", ps_df$pS))
ps_df$color <- ifelse(ps_df$pS < 0.05, 0, ps_df$pS)

ggplot(ps_df, aes(x = Comparison_A, y = Comparison_B, fill = color)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#4363BF", high = "#F9F0A1",
                      limits = c(0, 0.4), name = "pS") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

# 6. Reproducibility

The analysis uses the public NHANES 2017-2018 files DEMO_J, SMQ_J and BMX_J.
We include 20+ adults, classify smoking with SMQ020 and SMQ040, and omit
participants with missing BMI only when calculating the statistics.

The compact cached counts were extracted from the original RDS results
calculated in R with the settings above. To rerun every subsampling test,
change calculate_ss to TRUE in the header and delete the corresponding local
RDS files, if they already exist. Saved results are reused in later renders. The original MATLAB results are included only as
historical numerical reference and are not needed to run this example.
